calls.body: The Red Wings are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Blues are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.

DET.head: We leaned Detroit’s way (56%), but St. Louis had other ideas.

STL.head: We had St. Louis as slight underdogs (44%), and they pulled it off.

surprises.head: St. Louis got even better looks than usual
surprises.body: St. Louis usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots, and Detroit usually allows more dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: St. Louis’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.9% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Snuggerud sparks the Blues back from two down
paras: Dalibor Dvorský got the scoring started for the Blues early in the first. The Blues went more than 26 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the first to midway through the second, even with a power play in that stretch. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season. J.T. Compher tied it up for Detroit midway through the first. Keegan Kolesar scored his first goal for Detroit just 41 seconds into the second to put the Red Wings ahead 2-1. Lucas Raymond stretched the lead to 3-1 midway through the period, but Jimmy Snuggerud pulled the Blues within one with 28 seconds left in the period. The third period was a wild one. Emmitt Finnie made it 4-2 for the Red Wings on the power play early in the period, and that was all they would get. Pavel Buchnevich and Justin Barron scored less than five minutes apart midway through the period to tie it 4-4. Aleksanteri Kaskimäki, in his 11th NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Alexey Toropchenko, just 18 seconds later to put the Blues ahead for good.

The Red Wings outshot the Blues 28-15, but the Blues’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Joel Hofer made 24 saves for the Blues, and John Gibson allowed five goals on 15 shots. The Blues moved to 7-6-1, fifth in the Central, while the Wings fell to 6-5-3, still last in the Atlantic.

items.text: Justin Faulk played his first game against St. Louis since leaving, and picked up an assist.
